subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change gateway-host exec private-LAN reachability semantics?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the missing diagnostic, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a security and product-policy choice automation should not make.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94045 after checks are refreshed, while leaving LAN access semantics unchanged.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent parity as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Keep this issue open only as related context and resolve private-network access through the broader security-policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94045 after checks are refreshed, while leaving LAN access semantics unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the exec runtime outcome path and current exec surface ownership.
